summary: Ultramath swarm STARTED and running: ultramath_start returned swarm smwgpu16s, members m1 and m2, model deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash, effort max, member_steps 60, minutes 60, dir .ultramath/smwgpu16s; status confirms both members running, m2 on direction d1 (the three quantitative hinges of MC120), m1 still registering. Then refereed both claims independently. MC120 accepted and strengthened: the common-positive set I is the open arc of width 180 - a; the empty residual forces W empty, and for residual size 1 it suffices to pick two directions in I separated by gamma(r) = 2 arcsin(1/(2r)) < 60 degrees for some r > 1 with r - 1 below the strip widths there, giving two points in W at distance exactly 1, which contradicts a.e. monochromaticity of W against weak properness on a positive angular arc. Two corrections: the uniform-width step is neither in the source nor needed (widths are pointwise), and 120 degrees is sufficient rather than sharp - since gamma(r) < 60 strictly, the endpoint a = 120 is covered too and the true criterion is quantitative. Equilateral collapse: the transmitted arithmetic fails for 2-element blocks (their union is at most 4) and holds for 3-element vertex blocks {i-1,i,i+1}, where union >= 5 iff the indices differ by 2 or 3 mod 6; under that hypothesis MC120 gives pairwise separation >= 120 and three arcs summing to 360 force exactly equilateral.

swarm.m1_assignment: uniform strip / open-set / a.e. argument plus every endpoint and empty-residual case
swarm.m2_assignment: a strictly stronger six-colour-specific geometric obstruction for the equilateral paired case

verified_results: GRADE [P] Theorem MC120-prime: let c be measurable and weak, x a centre, K_i a finite family with ApproachingContinuum x (K i) v i whose directions lie in a closed cone of aperture a <= 120 degrees, H_i the excluded label sets, J = [k] minus the union of the H_i. If |J| <= 1 and W = intersection_i Straddle (K i) is nonempty, then False. Proof: I = {t : all inner products with v i positive} is the open arc of width 180 - a >= 60 degrees; pick beta' in I and r > 1 with r - 1 < delta(beta'); since gamma(r) = 2 arcsin(1/(2r)) < 60 degrees strictly, choose beta in I at angular separation gamma(r); the two points x + r e(beta) and x + r e(beta') are exactly unit apart by the chord formula and both lie in W (each in its own one-sided strip); a.e. points of W have colour j by the support exclusions, while weak properness gives different colours for a.e. point of the unit circle about a.e. point of W, and the circle meets W in a positive angular arc. Contradiction.

GRADE [P] Empty and singleton residual cases: if J is empty then no point of the nonempty open W can have a colour, so W = empty; the theorem must therefore carry W nonempty (or conclude W = empty). If |J| = 1 the argument above applies verbatim.

GRADE [P] Correction 1: the source supplies the outer-strip width delta pointwise (finite_positive_lower_bound is applied at a fixed direction inside ae_of_locally_ae) with no continuity in the direction, so a uniform positive width over a compact subarc is not established; the proof needs only positivity at the two chosen directions, and choosing r close to 1 makes the requirement r - 1 < delta satisfiable for both.

GRADE [P] Correction 2: the aperture 120 degrees is a sufficient bound, not the threshold. Since gamma(r) < 60 degrees strictly for every r > 1, the endpoint a = 120 is covered as well, and more generally a contradiction follows whenever some admissible radius r satisfies gamma(r) < 180 - a. So the sharp statement is quantitative rather than an aperture inequality.

GRADE [P] Correction 3 (equilateral collapse): two adjacent 2-element label blocks {i,i+1}, {j,j+1} have union size 4 - |intersection| <= 4, so they cannot cover 5 labels; the transmitted arithmetic is false for edge blocks and correct for 3-element VERTEX blocks B_i = {i-1, i, i+1}, where |B_s union B_t| >= 5 iff the vertex indices differ by 2 or 3 mod 6.

GRADE [P] Theorem EC-prime (equilateral collapse, corrected): for a measurable weak 6-colouring, three continua at a common centre whose excluded sets are vertex blocks with pairwise union of size at least 5 have pairwise direction separation at least 120 degrees, and hence their three directions are exactly 120 degrees apart. Proof: MC120-prime applied to each pair, then three consecutive arcs summing to 360 degrees with each at least 120 forces each to equal 120.

GRADE [C] Bank facts used without re-derivation: CC60 (closed 60-degree cone cannot leave at most 2 colours; paper accepted, Lean ongoing) and the sharpness of the generic finite-k angle-60 statement (accepted Borel 20-colour counterexamples for wider apertures, which do not settle k = 6). R4 and the fixed/moving three-centre replacements pass local Lean; full integration pending; no global chromatic bound and no 6-colouring.
conjectures: The equilateral configuration of three vertex-block continua is rigid but not excluded by CC60 plus MC120; a six-colour-specific obstruction would have to use the actual angular positions of the three blocks relative to the cycle labels, since equilateral leaves no slack in the direction parameter.

The sharp MC120 criterion is a comparison between the chord length at an admissible radius and the width of the common-positive arc, so any improvement must come from lower-bounding the strip widths delta, which in turn depends on how the K_i approach x (the size of the r_n and the deviation of w_n from v i).

If the endpoint and quantitative refinements hold up under review, the CC60 plus MC120 pair covers every configuration whose direction spread is at most 120 degrees with at most 1 residual label, and the remaining six-colour cases are exactly the three-block equilateral ones and the 2-residual families.
